title: Quantum Zeno and Anti-Zeno Responses: Universal Spectral Criterion for Measurement-Induced Decay
authors: Yu-Xiang Chen, Yuan-De Jin, Wen-Long Ma
abstract: We develop a general framework for characterizing the response of an evolving quantum system to repetitive quantum measurements. Modeling each evolution-measurement cycle as a quantum channel induced by an effective Liouvillian generator, we find that the Liouvillian spectral gap determines the measurement-induced decay rate. We analyze how the spectral gap responds to the measurement frequency, and define a quantum Zeno response as a decrease in the gap with increasing measurement frequency, and an anti-Zeno response as the opposite. We illustrate this criterion for both discrete-time and continuous-time quantum measurements. In an exactly solvable discrete-time qubit model, the exceptional-point spectral coalescence or spectral crossings mark the transition between Zeno and anti-Zeno responses, which can be experimentally distinguished from the long-time decay envelope of the survival probability. In a continuous-time superconducting-qubit defect model, the same transition manifests as smooth extrema of the spectral gap. Our results establish a universal spectral criterion for measurement-induced decay, offering a practical route to identify and manipulate these effects in generic quantum systems.
summary: This paper establishes a universal spectral criterion based on the Liouvillian spectral gap to characterize measurement-induced decay in quantum systems. It defines Zeno and Anti-Zeno responses by analyzing how this gap changes with measurement frequency. The framework is successfully applied to both discrete-time qubit and continuous-time superconducting qubit models, providing a general tool for quantum control.
main_problem: The paper develops a general framework to characterize how the decay rate of a quantum system changes when subjected to repetitive quantum measurements, addressing the Quantum Zeno and Anti-Zeno effects.
main_result: The measurement-induced decay rate is universally determined by the Liouvillian spectral gap, and the Zeno/Anti-Zeno transition is marked by spectral coalescence at Exceptional Points or smooth extrema of this gap.
method: The analysis models the evolution-measurement cycle using an effective Liouvillian generator, deriving a spectral criterion based on the derivative of the spectral gap with respect to the measurement frequency.
model_or_system: The framework is tested on two models: a discrete-time qubit undergoing periodic measurements (Ramsey interferometry) and a continuous-time superconducting-qubit defect model.
key_observables: The Liouvillian spectral gap ($\Gamma$), the response function $R = -\partial\Gamma / \partial f$, and the survival probability $P(m)$.
important_parameters: Measurement frequency ($f$ or $\gamma_\phi$), evolution time ($	au$), and measurement time ($	au_A$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximating the measurement process using effective Liouvillian generators and considering short-time or weak-measurement limits.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the cycle structure, the role of the effective generator, and show how the spectral gap's response $R$ changes across parameter regimes, demarcating Zeno ($R>0$) and anti-Zeno ($R<0$) regions via Exceptional Points.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general framework using effective Liouvillians, then applies this to specific models (discrete-time qubit and continuous-time superconducting qubit), deriving the spectral criterion and demonstrating the transition mechanisms.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, universal spectral diagnostic tool to predict and understand non-trivial dynamics (Zeno/Anti-Zeno) in open quantum systems, which is crucial for quantum control and measurement theory.
